On the Grass Fields any time

The Twin Houses: two tracks, one each, and one for what you build together; then the Lakeside power station for Tier 4. They are no part of the build order. The map draws every wall, window and railing; The base in the Plan panel sets how much of it shows, and Level shows one storey at a time.

For everybody on the server

Mouse and keys while editing

A piece in hand: click sets one down, press and drag lays a row of walls or a whole floor, R turns it, Esc or a right-click lets go, the middle button on a piece that stands takes one like it. Alt and drag moves the map.

Drag a piece to move it; drag the round handle to turn it. A floor takes what stands on it along (Shift: the floor alone). R a quarter turn (Shift: back), [ and ] 5° (Shift: 1°), arrows 1 m (Shift: 8 m, Alt: 10 cm), Ctrl D copy, Delete take out, G grid or free, Ctrl Z undo, Ctrl Y redo.

Lines: B belt, P pipe, L power line, V back to moving. Click each corner; a corner lands on a port near it, and a belt that reaches an inlet is done. An end on a port stays on it when the machine moves. Shift keeps it straight, Backspace takes the last corner back, double-click or Enter ends the line, Esc drops it.

Levels: a floor's card has Floor above for a roof or the next storey; every piece's card has its level in metres.

About

The positions of 7,695 things come from the Satisfactory Calculator map data for the base game: 481 ore nodes, 149 wells and geysers, 1,242 Power Slugs, 298 Mercer Spheres, 106 Somersloops, 118 crash sites and 5,301 plants. Satisfactory Plus renames six ores and keeps the nodes where they are. What a crash site asks for is the base game's answer.

Live data comes from the SatMap mod on this PC, at 127.0.0.1:8765. Joined to a dedicated server, the game gives a player no list of what is collected, so the map uses what the mod itself saw and what you tick by hand. Ticks and pins are kept in this browser.
